title: Introducing PicklStack — Stack Your Game
content:
## The Problem

We've all been there. You show up to open play, someone grabs a clipboard, and the next 45 minutes are a mess of **"who's played the most?"**, **"did Sarah already play twice?"**, and **"wait, when did Mike last get on court?"**

Manual queueing is slow, unfair, and kills the vibe. That's why we built **PicklStack**.

## What is PicklStack?

PicklStack is a free, web-based queueing and matchmaking system designed specifically for pickleball open play sessions. It handles the hard part — **fair court rotation, skill-balanced teams, and real-time tracking** — so you can focus on playing.

Create a session, check in players, and let the algorithm do the rest.

## How It Works

### 1. Create a Session
Set the number of courts, choose a matching mode, and give your session a name. It takes less than 30 seconds.

### 2. Check In Players
Add players one by one or import a list. Assign star ratings (1-5) to reflect skill levels. The algorithm uses these to create balanced matches.

### 3. Start Matches
Tap **GO** on any court. PicklStack instantly picks the next 4 players based on skill balance, wait time, and how many games each person has played.

### 4. Record Results
When a match ends, enter the score. The system updates rankings, tracks streaks, and picks the next group — all automatically.

## Key Features

### Skill-Balanced Matchmaking
Teams are paired so every game is competitive. No more stacked teams where one side dominates.

### Fair Court Time
The algorithm guarantees **equal rotation**. Everyone plays the same number of games, whether you're a 2-star or a 5-star player.

### No Repeat Opponents
In **Casual mode**, you'll never face the same opponent twice until everyone has played. This keeps games fresh and fun.

### Live Spectator View
Share a live link so friends, family, or other players can follow the action in real time — courts, queue, leaderboards, and all.

### Real-Time Leaderboard
Track wins, losses, win rate, and streaks as the session progresses. See who's on fire and who's due for a comeback.

## Get Started

No sign-up. No download. Just create a session and start playing.

**[Create your first session →](/create)**
excerpt: Tired of unfair court rotation and messy clipboards? Meet PicklStack — a free, smart queueing system for pickleball open play. Fair matchmaking, equal court time, and live spectator views.

title: From Clipboard to Cloud: Our Real-World Experience with PicklStack
content:
## The Morning of Our First Test

It was a Saturday morning at Riverside Community Court. Four courts, twenty-two players, and a whole lot of energy. We had been building PicklStack for months, but we had never used it in a real open play session with real players. Today was the day.

We set up a laptop on a folding table near the courts, opened PicklStack, and hit **Create Session**. Within 30 seconds, we had four courts configured, a matching mode selected, and a shareable join link ready to go.

## The Check-In Chaos (That Wasn't)

With a clipboard, this is where things usually fall apart. Someone can't spell their name, the organizer forgets to ask about skill level, and five people are standing around waiting while you figure out the paperwork.

With PicklStack, players scanned a QR code on their phones and checked themselves in. They typed their name, tapped their star rating, and they were in the queue. No clipboard. No waiting. No confusion.

**22 players checked in within 8 minutes.** With a clipboard, that would have taken 20.

## First Matches: The Moment of Truth

We tapped **GO** on Court 1. The algorithm picked four players — two 3-stars and two 2-stars, with balanced wait times. The teams were even. The game was competitive. Nobody got steamrolled.

We tapped **GO** on Courts 2, 3, and 4. Same result. Balanced teams, fair rotation, no repeats.

One player, who usually sits out for 30 minutes at open play, was on court within the first rotation. He looked at the queue on his phone and said, **"Wait, I'm already next? That never happens."**

That was the moment we knew this was working.

## The Live View: A Game Changer

We projected the live spectator view on a TV near the courts. Players could walk up and see:

- Which courts had active matches
- Who was in the queue and their position
- The current leaderboard
- Who was up next

It eliminated the constant **"When do I play?"** questions. Players could check their phones and see exactly where they stood. The organizer could focus on running the session instead of answering the same question twenty times.

## The Fairness Factor

Here's something we didn't expect: **players noticed the fairness immediately.**

After the third rotation, someone said, "This is the first time I've played four games at open play without having to argue about it." Another player mentioned that she usually gets paired with the same two people every time — today she played with eight different partners and opponents.

That's the power of algorithmic matchmaking. It's not just about efficiency. It's about **making sure everyone gets a fair shot.**

## When Things Got Real

Around the two-hour mark, we had a situation. A player had to leave early, and two new players arrived. With a clipboard, this would have been a headache — crossing names out, re-sorting the queue, figuring out who owed who a game.

With PicklStack, we removed the departing player from the queue, checked in the two new arrivals, and the algorithm automatically adjusted. The next matches were recalculated in seconds. No drama. No confusion.

## The Numbers

After three hours of play:

- **47 matches completed**
- **22 players** each played between 4 and 6 games
- **Zero disputes** about fairness or rotation
- **Average wait time** between games: 8 minutes
- **Longest wait**: 14 minutes (for a player who arrived late)

With our old clipboard system, the same session would have had:
- Around 35 matches (we lose 10-15 minutes per session to manual sorting)
- Some players would have played 7 games, others only 2
- At least 3-4 arguments about who was next
- Average wait time: 15-20 minutes

## What Players Said

We asked for feedback at the end of the session. Here are some highlights:

> "I don't know how I'm going back to the clipboard after this."

> "The fact that I played with different people every game was awesome. Usually I just play with the same 4 people."

> "I loved being able to see the queue on my phone. No more standing around wondering when I'm up."

> "The leaderboard was fun. It made people actually try harder."

> "This should be at every open play. Seriously."

## What We Learned

### 1. The Algorithm Works
We were nervous about whether the matchmaking would actually create balanced games. It did. Every single match was competitive. The star rating system, combined with wait time and game count, produced fair teams consistently.

### 2. Players Want Transparency
When people can see the queue, the rankings, and who's playing next, they trust the system. There's no suspicion that the organizer is playing favorites or that someone cut the line. Everything is visible.

### 3. The Live View Reduces Organizer Fatigue
Running open play with a clipboard is exhausting. You're constantly answering questions, updating the list, and making judgment calls. With PicklStack, the organizer becomes more of a facilitator than a gatekeeper.

### 4. New Players Feel Welcome
When someone new shows up, they used to have to awkwardly ask "How does this work?" and hope someone explains it. With PicklStack, they scan a QR code, check in, and the system tells them exactly what to do. The barrier to entry dropped to almost zero.

## What's Next

We're building more features based on what we learned:

- **Club Raid Mode** — for when multiple clubs come together for inter-club play
- **Advanced Stats** — head-to-head records, partner compatibility, and more
- **Tournament Bracket Support** — for when open play gets competitive
- **Custom Branding** — clubs can add their logo and colors to their sessions

## Try It Yourself

The best way to understand the experience is to try it. Create a session, invite some players, and see the difference for yourself.

No sign-up. No cost. Just better pickleball.

**[Start your session →](/create)**
